subject.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy

question: Should Codex heartbeat, cron, and inter-session turns carried on the internal WebChat marker be treated as unbound for cross-provider message authorization?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and restores pre-regression delivery, but returning no provider binding deliberately changes the default-deny security decision for autonomous message sends; code and tests cannot establish the intended trust boundary.

options.title: Approve the narrow exemption
options.body: Confirm these internal turn classes are not real conversation contexts and merge the branch with its retained WebChat-user containment tests.

options.title: Keep default deny
options.body: Retain provider binding for autonomous turns and require operators to opt into cross-provider delivery through existing configuration, accepting the documented workflow regression.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow exemption
recommendation.body: Confirm these internal turn classes are not real conversation contexts and merge the branch with its retained WebChat-user containment tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work by this owner defines Codex message-tool behavior during internal turns in the same runtime surfaces.
